_readme: Judgements the weekly sweep must not make again. Without this file scripts/discover.mjs
re-proposes everything anyone ever decided against, once a week, forever.
declined[] — a plugin that was looked at and deliberately not listed. `plugin` is either
'owner/repo' for a single-plugin repo or 'owner/repo/plugins/name' for one inside a
monorepo, lowercase. A reason is required: the next person to read this is deciding
whether the decision still holds, and 'no' on its own does not tell them.
listedAs[] — a plugin that IS in README.md under a name the sweep cannot match to its
directory. Only needed when the entry text and the folder disagree.
Nothing here is permanent. A plugin declined for being unfinished belongs in the list once
it is finished — delete the entry and the next sweep will propose it again.
MIRRORS. The same plugin can appear in several repos, and a copy passes every check —
it builds, it installs, its manifest is valid. So provenance is judged separately:
list the repo the copies name as their SOURCE (or the earliest to exist) and decline
the mirrors here, with the upstream named in the reason. Identical `name` + `version`
plus a matching hash of the entry file is enough to establish it. Declining a mirror
is not a judgement on the copier — it points readers at the maintainer.

declined.reason: Its own package.json description opens 'WORK IN PROGRESS — unfinished and unsupported'. The author is saying not to depend on it yet; the list should not say otherwise. Remove this entry when that wording goes.

Real plugin, well built (SQLite control plane, FTS5 memory, reviewed pipeline with one-use approvals, 21 agent tools, 71 test files), and nothing else on the list drives bb from Telegram. Declined on trust: there is NO LICENSE file at all, and the repo was two days old with 6 commits when read. It hands whoever holds a Telegram chat full-permission shell and bb CLI across every connected machine — its own README says to use a disposable repo for the first live run. Re-propose once it has a license, 'private' removed, and a real commit history. [Corrected 2026-08-15: this decline originally also cited private: true as blocking installation. That is false — private only gates npm publish, verified against the installer's own steps. The licence and history grounds stand on their own.]

The author disqualifies it: the README badge reads 'status: personal · unsupported' and 'Not published to npm. Personal tooling, unsupported for external use... written against one specific dotfiles repository layout. Against a differently shaped repo, every row reads missing and every task fails.' package.json is 'private: true'. The file registry and fourteen mise task names are hardcoded to that author's repo, so a stranger installs a panel of red 'missing' badges. Not a code-quality complaint.

Not a plugin — an internal shared library. package.json is 'private: true', has no bb key, declares no server or app surface, and carries @bb/plugin-sdk only as a devDependency for types; index.ts exports one factory. The repo's own packages/README.md calls it 'the shared idle-episode queue used by Improve Prompt and Design Doctrine'. Genuine engineering (1085 lines plus 609 of vitest), just not something a reader can install. The actual plugins in that repo are listed separately.

Its central claim does not hold. The pitch is many threads per branch/worktree, but the sidebar's '+ New thread in this workspace' calls openNewThread({projectId}) with no environment seed, so the thread lands wherever bb would have put it anyway; createWorkspaceFromLinear spawns into project-default rather than an issue-named worktree. The README lists both as the top unfinished items and docs/IMPLEMENTATION-NOTES.md opens 'Must validate against a live BB install'. v0.1.0-alpha.1, all 22 commits inside a ten-minute window on 2026-08-08, no tests, no CI. Re-propose once the existing-environment spawn works and it has run against a live bb.

Overwhelmingly a vendored fork of the Tasks plugin bb already ships, and it keeps upstream's identity rather than sitting beside it: it registers a CLI literally named 'tasks' with the same 15 subcommands and a navPanel id 'tasks'/title 'Tasks'/icon 'ListTodo', so installing it collides with a plugin every bb install already has enabled. The import commit landed 113 files and +49,126 lines; file-for-file diffs against get-bb/bb plugins/tasks are near-identical (tasks-editor.tsx 642 lines both sides, 6 differing lines, all import-path rewrites). Upstream is MIT and the LICENSE was dropped; upstream's tests were deleted. The author's own additions (Jira source, Beads source, execution engine, ~5,700 lines) are real — extracted as a plugin that composes with bb's Tasks instead of replacing it, that would be a different and plausibly listable thing.

Real plugin, genuinely distinct (cross-provider delegation to child threads with per-worker provider/model/effort, seven agent tools, a reconciler, 70 tests checked against deliberate mutations). Declined only on trust-for-a-stranger: the README has a '## Status' section reading 'Prototype' which discloses that orchestra_tell and the panel's '+ New' have never run against a live provider and that the 'bb plugin install git:' line it gives readers has not been tested end to end — that is the first thing a reader from this list would run, on full-trust code. 5 commits all on 2026-08-07, nothing since, no LICENSE. A verified git install plus a few weeks of the repo staying alive flips this; it would go under Threads & workflow.

Both headline invariants are genuinely implemented (no filesystem write path in server.ts at all; a run is recorded as 'refused' when the sealed manifest hash drifts). Declined on maintenance and scope: the README says 'This plugin is a prototype living in a personal fork for now' and plans to propose it upstream into bb within about a week, which would make a list entry stale by design; two commits, both 2026-08-07, no CI. Its 'bb evals check' is also hardcoded to one private knowledge base's layout (00-OPS/AGENTS-LOG.md, 01-ARCHITECTURE/ADRs/, a bespoke commit-message regex), so the deterministic layer does not apply to a stranger's repo.

A vendored copy of a plugin bb already ships. Its own README opens 'A customisable build of BB's Tasks plugin... Upstream source is vendored byte-for-byte', and .upstream-ref names ymichael/bb, tag desktop-v0.35.1, path official-plugins/tasks. package.json is 'private: true', the plugin id 'tasks' is reserved by the bundled one, and the documented install is 'cp -R ~/.bb/plugins/tasks/ ~/.bb/plugins/tasks-kv/' plus 'bb plugin disable tasks' — hand-migrating the builtin's live task database. The work on top (task dependencies/blocking plus subtask views, ~6,500 lines with vitest coverage) is real; re-propose if it ships standalone with its own plugin id and no manual data migration.

Not Web Push: no service worker, no VAPID, no push subscription. It is a 2.5s poll against an in-memory ring buffer in the server process (lost on restart) driving the foreground Notification API, so nothing arrives unless a bb tab is open. The README says so honestly; the repo NAME does not, and the entry would sit directly under bb-plugin-ios-notifications, which is actual Web Push. Also created 2026-08-11 with 4 commits, no LICENSE, and its own settings UI says 'Phase 1 delivers notifications while BB is open in this browser'. Code quality is good (strict TS, zod-validated RPC, vitest, green CI). Worth re-proposing with commits behind it, ideally under a name that does not say 'web push'.

Substantial and real (~3,500 lines, SHA-256 compare-and-swap on every agent write, dictation through bb's own voice-transcription endpoint, four CLI subcommands, three app slots, a genuine test suite) and distinct from the Editing & files entries. Declined on maintenance, in the author's own words: the single commit that introduces it (e7473a6, 2026-08-09) is a multi-package checkpoint whose body reads 'Also includes in-flight WIP: bb-plugin-grove...'. That is the package's entire history — no follow-up, no iteration. Its README install command is also hardcoded to /Users/patrick/workingdir/. Re-propose once it has history beyond the checkpoint that called it in-flight.

Not a plugin for bb. Every server call goes through bb.sdk.sessionFabric, a capability that exists only in the author's own fork (pierback/bb, forked from get-bb/bb 2026-08-11). Generating the SDK declarations against bb 0.37.0 gives zero occurrences of sessionFabric, so requireSessionFabricCapability() throws on load and the plugin does nothing on a real bb; its engines.bb is '>=0.36 <0.37', which the current release does not satisfy either. The README states it requires 'Pierback BB 0.36.x' and 'deliberately has no fallback for upstream BB builds'. Reconsider if sessionFabric lands in upstream bb.

Installs and builds, but the manifest sets bb.server to "./dist/server.js" — a committed 914 KB build artifact — so the code bb loads is the checked-in blob, not the 11k lines of source beside it. Deleting dist/ and rebuilding fails outright ("manifest bb.server points at a missing file"), which is what showed the artifact is load-bearing rather than incidental. For full-trust code on a directory whose own header says "read the source before installing", that is the wrong shape. There is also no LICENSE file, and the README documents a governance contract ("contract v9/schema v10", one-request operator receipts) rather than what a user gets. Point bb.server at source, add a license, and re-propose.

Not installable. server.ts:3 imports zod, but zod sits in devDependencies, and `bb plugin install git:` runs `npm install --omit=dev` — so the build dies on `Could not resolve "zod"`. Reproduced in a fresh clone on 2026-08-15. One line in package.json fixes it. Also has no LICENSE, and typescript / react-dom / @types/react-dom are in dependencies where they do not belong. The plugin itself — a Files panel with per-file tabs and TS/JS go-to-definition — looks like real work; re-propose once it installs.

Not installable, same one-line cause as sudohackin/bb-plugin-change-review: server.ts:23 imports zod while zod is in devDependencies, so the managed install (npm install --omit=dev) cannot resolve it and `bb plugin build` fails. Reproduced in a fresh clone on 2026-08-15; the committed dist/ hides this locally but does not survive the installer. Nothing else against it — 15k lines, tests, honest secret settings. Worth knowing before installing: sprite generation calls api.openai.com, and optionally api.retrodiffusion.ai, with your own key. Move zod to dependencies and this is a straightforward yes under Fun.

Not installable — the third plugin caught by the same one-line bug in three days. server.ts:30 imports zod while zod sits in devDependencies, and `bb plugin install git:` runs `npm install --omit=dev`, so the build dies on `Could not resolve "zod"`. Reproduced in a fresh clone of v0.1.2 (55032b4) on 2026-08-17. Nothing else against it: MIT, 2.3k lines, seven real commits, and the author already has Dispatch and Lanes on the list, both of which install fine. Move zod to dependencies and it goes straight into Threads & workflow. Reported upstream as slogsdon/bb-plugin-global-workflows#1 on 2026-08-17.

Real and substantial (634-line Unix-socket bridge, Zod-validated NDJSON, one chokepoint for every pi consumer plugin), but the lane it heads requires `scripts/patch-pi-bridge.mjs`, which rewrites bb's OWN installed `bb-pi-bridge.mjs` to inject env wiring and must be re-run after every bb update. The author documents that plainly and the patch is idempotent with a `--revert`, but a directory should not point strangers at patching the host app. The same reason covers its three pi consumers, listed separately. Re-propose if the bridge works without patching bb.
Depends on bb-plugin-pi-events-bridge, whose install patches bb's own bundled `bb-pi-bridge.mjs`. Declined for the same reason as the bridge, not on its own quality.

Real plugin (396 lines, node:os and statfs sampling, SQLite `samples` table with 1d/7d/30d buckets), declined for overlap: CPU, memory, disk and load on the bb host is already MGrin/bb-plugin-system's entry, and 30 days of history in SQLite is not enough daylight for a second entry in the same section. Its sibling Skills.sh is listed.

Real implementation (697-line server shelling out to the third-party `asc` CLI, nav panel and thread action, TestFlight notes and group writes), but its own README and `skills/example-skill/SKILL.md` are still untouched `bb plugin new` scaffold text, so it reads as unfinished. Re-propose when the docs are written. Its sibling ios-simulators is listed.

Works — fetches the OpenCode Zen Go usage endpoint with a Bearer key resolved from settings, env or `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`, and adds a `bb opencode-go usage` CLI — but not distinct: Lanes already normalises OpenCode Zen Go headroom into its gauges, and the list already carries six usage plugins. Its sibling ios-simulators is listed.
At 0.x and absent from the repo's own `marketplace.json`, so the author has not published it. The repo IS listed, on its three mobile-web fixes. Re-propose when it ships a release.

A fork of a plugin the list already carries upstream (SawyerHood/bb-plugin-t3sidebar and smsunarto's GTD Sidebar, both listed). A directory that points at three copies of one plugin is worse than one that points at the original.
A fork of MateoCerquetella's usage-tracker, which is already listed; its LICENSE still carries Mateo Cerquetella's copyright. Listed upstream, not here.

A vendored copy of somebody else's plugin: package.json declares name `@smsunarto/bb-plugin-gtd-sidebar` version 0.4.1, byte-for-byte the version smsunarto publishes to npm, and it landed here in a single commit on 2026-08-24. The upstream is already listed under smsunarto/bb-plugins. Nothing against the code — it is not this repo's plugin to list.

Too thin: `server.ts` is `export default function plugin(_bb) {}` and the whole plugin is one content script adding a Copy session ID row to the sidebar context menu. Real and harmless, but there is no entry to write that a reader would act on. Re-propose if it grows.

Nobody but the author can install it. `@get-bb/plugin-sdk` is a devDependency pinned to `file:./vendor/get-bb-plugin-sdk-0.4.15.tgz`, `vendor/` is gitignored and not committed, so `npm install` on a clean clone dies with ENOENT — measured — which kills both the README's own quick-install and the `bb plugin install git:` form. The README blames npm for not carrying 0.4.15, which is no longer true (0.4.15 published 2026-08-23, 0.4.16 on 2026-08-24). The plugin itself is strong — a bead DAG in SQLite, graph routing, hidden worker threads per bead, a review gate, a mirror onto the builtin tasks plugin — so re-propose the moment that devDependency points at the published SDK.

Does not do what it claims. The headline is ghost text you accept with one key; there is no keyboard handling anywhere in the repo — `ghostAcceptKeys` and `displayMode` are plumbed through settings, config, store and RPC and nothing consumes them, and app.tsx renders the same Accept/Dismiss card either way, citing a content script the package.json does not declare and the tree does not contain. `bb suggester enable/disable` mutates an in-process variable and never writes settings, so it resets on reload. The README's own `install …@v0.1.0` points at a tag that does not exist (zero tags, zero releases). It is also only narrowly distinct from bb-plugin-next-steps, already listed, which implements the key-accept this one advertises.

Mostly other people's code. The provider half is bb's own builtin `provider-acp` bridge vendored nearly verbatim and pointed at `opencode2 acp` (diffed against the shipped source map: 0 differing lines in visibility.ts, 2 in profiles.ts, 2 in tool-call-operation.ts); the usage half is a fork of MateoCerquetella's usage-tracker, already listed, whose LICENSE still reads Copyright Mateo Cerquetella. The one new thing, "native skill routing", is 27 lines that rewrite `/name` into an English sentence asking the model to use OpenCode's skill tool — a prompt nudge, not tool routing. It also ships unused vendored credential-reading code (`src/bridge/provider-maintenance.ts` reads Cursor keychain and auth tokens; nothing imports it) inside full-trust code that launches a local CLI. Three commits, all 2026-08-23. Re-propose if the vendored bridge thins out.

Listed on 2026-08-25 and removed on 2026-08-31: bb absorbed it. get-bb/bb#2127 'Ship the Monaco editor as a builtin plugin' merged 2026-08-25T23:06:45Z, and 24 minutes later the author committed 'Mark the plugin deprecated in the README' and archived the repo — the README now says outright that recent bb versions ship Monaco out of the box and the plugin is no longer maintained. Confirmed on this machine: bb 0.40.0 carries builtin:monaco-editor@0.1.0, so installing this would duplicate a bundled plugin, which is the same ground as the vendored-copy declines. Nothing was wrong with the plugin. Do not re-propose unless bb drops the builtin.

Real plugin and it works, but bb-plugin-copilot (balazstasi) is already listed and does the same job: same provider id acp-copilot, same `copilot --acp` launch, same managed ACP entry, same needs-configuration on a missing CLI. The genuine difference is version currency, not function — this one writes the provider-acp plugin's `customAgents` setting and strips the deprecated `customAcpAgents` array that bb 0.41 removes — which is a swap decision for the list owner, not a second Providers row saying the same sentence twice. Also thin for full-trust code that writes another plugin's settings: 6 commits over 4 days, 0 stars, no LICENSE, four of six commits authored by coding agents. It carries the listed entry's PATH caveat worse — findBinary() only checks accessSync(path, X_OK) with no `--version` probe, so any executable named `copilot` is registered, including the unrelated AWS ECS Copilot CLI. One live bug: `existing.command.includes(delimiter)` tests for the PATH list separator, so the reuse branch is dead on macOS and Linux. Re-propose as a REPLACEMENT for the listed entry once bb 0.41 makes the config.json path fail.

Real, competent, MIT, and distinct — nothing in Host & environment clones a disposable VM and enrols it as a bb host. Declined on maturity, on the author's own words: version 0.2.0-alpha.1, README says 'Status: early alpha ... It has not yet been exercised against a production exe.dev account' and 'A production run with real bb and exe.dev credentials remains required before a stable release'; SPEC.md still lists incomplete orphan GC and pushed-branch detection, and says the exe.dev API was checked against documentation, not against the API. The tests are real but run entirely against createFakePluginHost with a stubbed fetch, so nothing here has provisioned or deleted a VM. That matters more than usual because the failure mode is spending money on cloud VMs and deleting them: a stranger installing it off this list would be the first to run the destroy path for real. Re-propose once the author reports a live smoke run and the alpha banner comes off.

The code is real and read-only as advertised, built on the SDK with no shelling out and tests on both halves. Declined on maintenance and, marginally, distinctness: the repo was created 2026-08-29T17:01:13Z and pushed ten seconds later, has exactly one commit, 0 stars, no LICENSE file anywhere, and a root package.json marked private — there is no maintenance record to judge and no licence, so a stranger cannot legally reuse it. The list already carries three file browsers (bb-plugin-files, bb-plugin-filetree, Server File Explorer); its honest distinction is spanning every project's configured sources plus the worktree environments of that project's threads across connected hosts, which is a real but narrow axis. Re-propose once the repo has history and a licence — the code is not the problem.

A vendored copy of a plugin bb already ships, which is an exclusion on its own. The first commit is 'Port BB's built-in tasks plugin as tasks-plus', forked at tag desktop-v0.40.0, and the README opens 'A personal fork of BB's built-in Tasks plugin'; package.json is private and v0.1.0, and the MIT LICENSE is upstream's, carried over with upstream's copyright holder. The added features are real (blocker relations with cycle detection, nested subtask rows, collapsible status groups, a task_artifacts table with CLI and detail-view surfaces) but they sit on a full copy of upstream, so installing it means disabling the builtin, hand-copying ~/.bb/plugins/tasks/data.db, and thereafter tracking upstream by manually diffing release tags and redoing five import rewrites — the README says so itself. 18 commits by one author over three days is not enough track record to ask a reader to swap out a bundled plugin.

An empty scaffold, not a working plugin. Both declared entry points have empty bodies — server.ts is `export default function plugin(_bb: BbPluginApi): void {}` and app.tsx is `definePluginApp(() => {})` — so it contributes no CLI command, tool, panel or notification. The README says so: 'This repository currently contains only the backend and frontend plugin scaffold. Notification behavior is intentionally out of scope for the initial setup.' It is also `private: true` with `license: UNLICENSED` and a LICENSE reading 'private and proprietary. No permission is granted to use, copy, modify, publish, distribute', so a reader who found it here could not legally install it. One commit ever (b8f346c, 2026-08-07, 'chore: scaffold BB notifications plugin'). Re-propose if the notification behaviour lands and the licence opens.

The provider is genuinely implemented (bb.providers.register over src/{binding,session,auth,storage,catalog}.ts with 11 test files), but it is not ready for a stranger: version 0.0.0, no README in the directory, zero `nanocodex/v*` tags on the remote so the documented git install cannot resolve a release, and its only devDependency is a pkg.pr.new commit-pinned preview build of nanocodex itself. Every other plugin this repo publishes is already listed. Re-propose once it is tagged, released and carries a README.

An explicit vendored fork of bb's builtin github plugin, which is an exclusion. Its own README states 'This plugin is a fork of bb's builtin github plugin, version 0.2.1' and tells you to `bb plugin disable github` first to avoid duplicate panels, mentions and CLI. The implementation is substantial and real (1736-line server, gh-CLI auth, 5-minute background sync into SQLite, zod-validated rpc contract) — the ground is the vendored-copy rule, not quality. It is also absent from the repo's own marketplace.json, so the author has not published it. Re-propose if it stops being a fork of the bundled plugin, or if bb drops the builtin.

Not installable. src/provider-bridge.ts:44 imports `@get-bb/plugin-sdk/provider-bridge`, but `@get-bb/plugin-sdk` is in devDependencies, so under `npm install --omit=dev` the package is absent and the build dies on `Could not resolve "@get-bb/plugin-sdk/provider-bridge"`. Worth noting for other authors: bb externalises the BARE `@get-bb/plugin-sdk` specifier at build time, which is why an SDK in devDependencies usually passes — this SUBPATH is not externalised, so the usual exemption does not apply and the SDK has to be a real dependency here. Reproduced in a fresh clone on 2026-09-01 against bb 0.40.0. Its three siblings in the same repo build clean and are listed.

Vendored snapshot, not the author's own plugin. The repo's own README carries a Source column naming upstream as patleeman/bb-plugins (packages/bb-plugin-prime-agent), refreshed by a `sync-plugins` automation. patleeman's prime-agent is already listed. Declining the mirror rather than the work: a directory should point at the maintainer, not at a copy.
Vendored snapshot, not the author's own plugin. The repo's README names upstream as MayankBansal12/bb-plugin-usage, which is already listed. Same reasoning as the prime-agent entry above.

Real plugin (definePlugin server, backfill/check commands, an auth:"local" HTTP route, a trace-pump background service, an app entry) and the repo is well maintained, but it has no release: `git ls-remote --tags` carries 29 tag refs in 8 families and NONE for agent-trace, so the documented `bb plugin install <id>` cannot resolve a version. Same ground as the nanocodex decline above. Re-propose once a tag is pushed — the code is not the problem.

The author disqualifies it: its own README opens with a WARNING saying it is experimental, has not been submitted to the marketplace, and requires matching BB core changes that are not released plus SDK 0.4.33. A stranger installing it today gets a plugin its author says will not work. Remove this entry when that warning goes.

A placeholder, not a plugin: server.ts is 2 lines and app.tsx is 6, holding a localStorage contract so a model choice survives until upstream BB PR #1964 lands. Its own README says it does not override bb's picker. Nothing for a reader to install and use. Re-propose if it grows into something after that PR.

Real plugin, carefully built — the RPC contract is fully implemented and the guest authz decision is deny-by-default, enforced in a Cloudflare worker that filters bb's bootstrap JSON and WebSocket frames. Declined on trust and readiness, not code. No LICENSE, no tag, no release; 90 commits in a 5-day burst then cold. The plugin's own README still calls it a "Scaffold" whose handlers "still throw not implemented", which is flatly false of the code that shipped, so a reader is misled about what they are installing. Its docs also record that the Cloudflare worker self-destructs 60 minutes after deploy unless manually claimed, and that a redeploy mints a new hostname invalidating every guest URL already handed out. And the access-control boundary is a CSS/DOM chrome shim pinned to bb 0.40.0 / commit 31a190d, so a bb upgrade degrades a security boundary rather than merely breaking a feature — while installing it grants a URL-holder live read or write into your threads. Re-propose once it has a licence, a release, and a README that matches the code.

The proposed repo is one person's personal agent configuration ("Personal coding-agent configuration and skills for Ryan Brown"), not a plugin repo, and the plugin inside it is not installable as published: package.json pins `engines.bbPluginSdk` 0.4.36, a version never published to npm (the registry goes 0.4.35 -> 0.4.40), so the repo commits a 512KB SDK tarball built from a local bb checkout, and its build/verify steps point outside the directory a --subdirectory install would fetch. It is also incomplete on its own — the workflow it exists to serve lives in the parent repo's skills/firstmate-queue/SKILL.md, which hardcodes the author's own /Users/ryanbrown/code path, so a stranger gets the panel and none of the convention. 12 commits over three days and no LICENSE anywhere in the repo. The code itself is competent; re-propose once it stands alone with a licence and a published SDK floor.

Real and does exactly what it claims — 15 lines subscribing to thread.created and pinning visible root threads, with tests. Declined on the same grounds as this repo's project-files above, which still hold: two commits total, 0 stars, and NO LICENSE file anywhere in the repo, so nobody has been granted the right to use it. Re-propose once the repo has a licence and some history — the code is not the problem.

The Codex login-slot switching core genuinely works (host.ts copies ~/.codex/auth.json into per-slot files and restores one atomically), but the plugin is not finished for anyone but its author. accounts_list always injects two hardcoded slots, "personal" and "work", backed by ~/.codex-personal/auth.json and ~/.codex-work/auth.json — the author's own machine layout, never mentioned in the README, and an error for everyone else. Most of the `bb plugin new` scaffold was never cleaned out: the manifest still calls it "Codex Capacity" with a ListTodo icon, most of the README is the untouched scaffold text about "a plugin that keeps a todo list", and skills/example-todos/SKILL.md tells agents to run `bb codex-capacity list|add|done`, a CLI server.ts never registers. One commit, no LICENSE, not on npm, dist/ gitignored. Re-propose once the scaffold leftovers and the hardcoded personal/work paths are gone and it has a licence.

A rename of a "usage" plugin with the identifiers left behind, and one of them is load-bearing: bb derives a plugin's id from the package name, so this installs as `multi-claude` while app.tsx hardcodes PLUGIN_ID = "usage" and fetches /api/v1/plugins/usage/rpc/getUsage — the entire UI half cannot reach its own RPC, and every RPC path and `bb plugin reload usage` line in the README points at the wrong plugin too. Two more: syncAcpConfig shells out `bb plugin config provider-acp set customAgents <its own array>` at every plugin start, overwriting whatever else registered there (bb-plugin-copilot, bb-auggie and bb-droid, all listed here, write into that same setting); and the env block it registers pins claude-sonnet-4-6/opus-4-6 while its wrapper advertises sonnet-5/opus-5/fable-5, so the model you pick is not the model that runs. One commit, no LICENSE despite the README claiming MIT, `bb plugin new` scaffold skill still in the tree, and a hardcoded /opt/homebrew/bin/claude-agent-acp path the author calls a thing auto-detection is "planned" for.

A fork of charpeni's Dependabot plugin, which is already listed. Its only original commit changes 47 lines of server.ts — zod length bounds on advisory metadata, an https://github.com/ allowlist on alert URLs, and the untrusted-data warning moved above the advisory text in the fix prompt — plus a LICENSE and a test. Good hardening, but a second entry would carry a description indistinguishable from the one already there, giving a reader no way to choose. The right home for the change is a PR to charpeni. MIRROR: upstream is charpeni/bb-plugins/plugins/dependabot.
